title: Unified Inference — Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release (2027-09)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary and purpose:

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap themes, pricing/packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family as of the 2027-09 release. It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer-facing orgs to align on scope, success metrics, and launch actions.

Context and problem statement:
- Customers expect a single, consistent inference API and operational model across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Key pain points we solve: unpredictable latency under load, fragmented model variant handling, lack of cost controls tied to workload characteristics, and complex on-prem delivery for regulated customers.

Goals (outcome-oriented):
1. Deliver a single API and rollout experience that supports model routing, cost-aware fallbacks, and structured responses across hosting modes.
2. Reduce median token cost for typical RLHF/chat workloads by 20% through batching, caching, and quantization guidance.
3. Achieve 99.95% availability for Hosted routes in our US and EU regions and provide enterprise SLAs for Dedicated customers.

Success metrics / KPIs:
- API availability (global hosted): 99.95% (SLO target)
- P95 generation latency (short prompts, 256 tokens): <= 150ms
- Token cost reduction (measured vs baseline): >= 20% for recommended workloads
- Adoption: 30 new Dedicated customers and 10 Private deals closed in the next 6 months after launch

Scope (what's included):
- Unified API surface for generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking.
- Model-routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, region-preferred, tier-based.
- Cost-aware fallbacks: automated substitution to quantized/near-compatible models when capacity constrained.
- Redwood Optimize integration: automated quantization recommendations and batching presets surfaced in Console.
- Developer SDK updates: streaming and function-calling improvements with structured output validation.

Out of scope (this release):
- New model training or fine-tuning-as-a-service.
- First-class support for specialized hardware types not in our current fleet (e.g., newest accelerator-gen) — will be added in a later roadmap item.

Functional requirements (PRD-level):
1. API: A single REST/SDK interface endpoint that supports the following features across environments:
   - text generation, chat (multi-turn), embeddings, and reranking.
   - streaming responses and chunked token events.
   - function/tool calling with schema-driven outputs.
2. Model Routing Engine:
   - Accept routing policy per request (header or route config).
   - Evaluate available variants and select the best candidate based on policy and recent capacity signals.
   - Support automatic fallback to quantized variants or different region when primary capacity is exceeded.
3. Cost Controls and Recommendations:
   - Expose per-route batching and caching settings in Console with recommended presets.
   - Provide a score and recommended quantization profile per model/workload (via Redwood Optimize).
4. Observability & Telemetry:
   - Per-request token counts, per-token latency, model-variant selected, cache hit/miss metrics.
   - Dashboards: Per-route cost breakdown (tokens, batching effect), error rates, tail latency.
5. Security & Compliance:
   - Maintain encryption-in-transit and at-rest for Private/Dedicated.
   - Key management integration (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments.
   - Audit logging for model selection changes and routing policy updates.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
- Throughput: support sustained 10k RPS aggregate for Hosted API in peak region with autoscale headroom.
- Latency: P95 <= 150ms for short generations; P99 tail safeguards with graceful degradation (fallback model or partial streaming).
- Reliability: error budget target aligned with 99.95% availability.
- Cost: per-token cost targets by workload class (see pricing section).

SLO / performance table (reference):
- Metric | Target
- Availability (Hosted API) | 99.95%
- P95 latency (256 tok) | <= 150ms
- P99 latency (256 tok) | <= 500ms (with fallback)
- Cache hit rate (prefix cache for chat) | >= 40% on repeat sessions

Design overview (high level):
- Components:
  - Unified Control Plane (Cloud): routing policy manager, model catalog, Optimize recommendations, billing hooks.
  - Serving Fleet (Edge/Region): model-serving pods with runtime that supports quantized execution and KV cache.
  - Router: a lightweight policy evaluator located in the region that chooses model variant and dispatches to the serving pod.
  - Client SDKs & Console: developer-facing SDKs, Console UI for route config and recommendations.
- Key patterns:
  - Continuous batching with dynamic magic-buckets: grouping by recent sequence-length distributions.
  - Prefix / KV cache layer that is region-local and warms on common prompt prefixes.
  - Kernel selection at load time to prefer quantized kernels when recommended.

API surface & UX notes:
- Backward compatible endpoints. Default behavior unchanged for existing customers.
- New optional headers: X-Redwood-Routing-Policy, X-Redwood-Cost-Preference, X-Redwood-Trace-Id.
- Console flows:
  1) Route creation wizard with recommended batching/cache presets.
  2) Optimize suggestions shown as one-click apply for quantization/batching.

Design specifications (developer-facing):
- Request schema example (JSON):
  {
    "model": "redwood-compat-3b",
    "input": "<chat payload>",
    "routingPolicy": "cost-first",
    "stream": true
  }
- Routing policy precedence: request header > route-level config > account default > global default.
- Fallback behavior: max 2 fallback hops (variant -> quantized variant -> region fallback).

Roadmap & themes (next 6 quarters):
- Q3 2027 (current release): Unified API, model-routing engine v1, Optimize integration, Console presets, GA for hosted routes.
- Q4 2027: Dedicated rollout automation, A/B rollouts for routing policies, expanded observability (trace linking).
- Q1 2028: Private on-prem wizard + hardened day-2 ops, extended hardware support, per-customer quantization training guidance.
- Q2 2028: Fine-grained cost SLOs, multi-tenant inference isolation primitives, self-serve Dedicated purchase.

Pricing & packaging notes (guidance for GTM & sales ops):
- Pricing model remains usage-based, with per-token generation pricing and per-embedding unit. New elements:
  - Routing premium: optional add-on for SLA-backed latency-first routing.
  - Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity with tiers (S, M, L) priced by committed GPU hours + platform fee.
  - Private: annual license + deployment fee + optional managed support.
- Example published price tiers (reference guidance to Sales):
  - Hosted Standard: $0.006 / 1k generation tokens; Embeddings: $0.0015 / embedding unit.
  - Hosted Optimize (recommended): 15% discount on tokens when customer applies Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization.
  - Dedicated S/M/L: contact Sales (estimate: $Xk/month for S, $Yk/month for M) — sales to reference internal pricebook.
- Bundles & promotions: 3-month free Optimize trial for new Hosted accounts; reduced onboarding fee for Private customers who commit to enterprise support.

Release notes (2027-09 release highlights):
- GA: Unified API for generation, chat, embeddings with streaming and function calling improvements.
- New: Model-routing engine v1 with latency- and cost-first policies.
- New: Redwood Optimize console recommendations surfaced inline with route config.
- Performance: measured 22% average token cost reduction across internal benchmark prompt-sets when recommendations applied.
- Observability: Per-route cost breakdown dashboard and trace linking in Console.
- Breaking changes: none. Default model behavior unchanged; new features opt-in via route config.

Rollout and migration plan:
1) Internal dogfooding: 2-week alpha across product and infra teams.
2) Limited beta: 10 customers (mix of Hosted and Dedicated) for 6 weeks, gather telem and feedback.
3) Gradual GA: staged by region (US -> EU -> APAC) with feature flags.
4) Migration guidance for customers: document showing how to opt into routing policies and Optimize recommendations (Console + API examples).

Operational runbook highlights (for eng-sre & eng-platform):
- Key alerts to add before GA: routing policy latency exceedance, fallback rate increase > 1% of requests, cache eviction storm.
- Suggested SRE playbook steps for fallback storms: 1) throttle new route config changes; 2) increase capacity in region; 3) temporarily set routing policy to region-preferred.

Open decisions and risk register:
- Decision: Max fallback hops = 2 (risk: potential quality regression on second hop) — mitigations: validate fallback model families and add regression guardrails.
- Risk: quantized models may produce subtle quality differences on few prompt-sets — mitigations: provide per-customer evaluation harness and explicit rollout gates.

Next steps (2-week actions):
- Finalize Console presets and One-Click Optimize apply flow (Product + Eng: 2 weeks).
- Complete Beta rollout and collect regression metrics on customer prompts (Applied ML: 3 weeks).
- Publish Sales kit and updated pricing reference (Sales enablement: 1 week).

Appendix A — API example (cURL):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/unified/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-compat-3b","input":"Summarize the following...","routingPolicy":"cost-first","stream":false}'
